title: Naked Lunch
author: William S. Burroughs
current_text: In November 1967, the Tribunal held Naked Lunch to be indecent in New Zealand. In February 1960, Customs seized an imported copy of Naked Lunch at Port Adelaide and banned it as “hard-core pornography.” US Customs embargoed Naked Lunch as allegedly obscene under the Tariff Act (1930). In a proceeding initiated by a petition filed on September 17, 1964, the Superior Court adjudged Naked Lunch obscene, but the final decree was reversed and a new decree was ordered declaring that the book could not be declared obscene.

sources.quote: WILLIAM Burroughs' The Soft Machine is the third of his novels to be submitted to the Tribunal. In 1964 Dead Fingers Talk was held to be not indecent, but in November 1967 Naked Lunch was held to be indecent.
sources.title: Page 668, No. 27, NZ Gazette 1971

sources.quote: First published in 1959 by Olympia Press, Paris, William Burroughs’ ‘Naked Lunch’ (sometimes ‘The Naked Lunch’) provides a fractured account of American homosexual and drug cultures in the 1950s. One of the most provocative and radical novels of the 20th century, it was banned as ‘hard-core pornography’ by Customs after an imported copy was seized at Port Adelaide in February 1960.

sources.quote: Drug-addiction, sexual fantasy, and cannibalism re-occur in William Burroughs' "Naked Lunch", first published by Olympia Press in Paris in 1959. Using the Tariff Act (1930), US Customs consistently embargoed this work as allegedly obscene.

ban_rows.note: Banned by Boston courts in 1962 for obscenity, but that decision was reversed in 1966 by the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court.
Declared indecent by the NZ Indecent Publications Tribunal in 1967; reclassified in September 1974 as indecent only in the hands of persons under 18.
Banned in Belarus by addition to the Official List of Publications Harmful to National Interests (Ministry of Information). Decision: 2025-09-30. Country of origin: USA. Documented by PEN Belarus.
